pr_body:
This PR brings `pinctrl` support to Espressif SoCs and their related boards.

It also removes `pinmux` support off Espressif SoCs.

This work links to #39740.

Closes #43715

issue_context.title: ESP32 UART devicetree binding design issue
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

Creating a bug from the discussion here:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/41941#discussion_r789262385

The espresssif,esp32-uart devicetree binding has a required `peripheral` property which specifies an index into the available UARTs.

This is a binding design problem because the index number is not hardware description: according to @sylvioalves , the value is not used to describe or configure hardware, and is present in the binding as a work-around for interfacing with the HAL-based zephyr UART shim driver for this peripheral. Such properties go against devicetree design principles.

**Expected behavior**

- The property should be removed from the binding
- Another hardware-appropriate workaround should be implemented in the shim driver

**Impact**

Annoyance

review_comments: Though, in general, it is good practice to keep variables restricted to the scope they are being used, here, I'd rather keep it out to avoid variable redefinitions or stack unwinding in different compiling optimization scenarios (including, eventually, debugging).
nit: this header makes use of `BIT()`, so it should include `<sys/util_macro.h>`
In this case, "BIT()" is also defined on Espressif's HAL.
I mean, header is not self-contained, this is a bad practice.
Right, I have updated it with the header inclusion.
